$comment: The source of sf-thread-list's element plumbing (core/js/element-manifest.js). Taken from simai/ui-control control/smart-architecture/migration/out/thread-list (migration/convert-1.3.8.mjs over simai/ui-pro@9cbe061); standard simai.smart-component 1.3.8, vocabulary 1.1.5. Every x-todo of the conversion is decided: x-decisions says how.

threads.x-markup: a property (a host has objects); newest first by updated-at, the pinned ones (pinned: true, Mirai24 API v1.1) first under their own heading «Закреплённые» with a quiet «Закреплён» line; pin and unpin are the host's row actions (apply); avatar is {image-url, text}; title, caption and avatar text are text, never markup. updated_at and avatar.image_url, the 1.0 spellings, are read until 2026-12-01 and noted

has-more.summary: A next page exists: reaching the end asks for it.

archived.summary: Show the archive: a way back, Restore instead of Archive, no New conversation.

no-manage.summary: No row actions: no menu, no F2.

no-archive.summary: No archive: no way to it and no Archive among the row actions.

group-by.summary: day: Today, Yesterday, Earlier by updated_at in the reader's time zone. none: one list.

label.summary: The navigation's accessible name; empty is Conversations, or Archive, in the page's language.

loading.x-summary: while the first page loads: the shape of the list instead of words (was setLoading)
loading.summary: The shape of the list while the first page loads.

status.x-summary: a sentence in place of the list, an error the host could not recover from; empty clears it (was setStatus)
status.summary: A sentence in place of the list (an error); empty clears it.

actions.x-summary: the host's own row actions after «Rename» and «Archive»; chosen, one leaves as apply {action, scope: entry, ids}

selected.summary: the open conversation; a press asks for it with open {id} and the host writes it back

open.summary: A conversation is asked for (vocabulary open); the host writes selected back. The 1.0 name sf-thread-list-select follows until 2026-12-01.

rename.summary: A conversation was renamed in place; the new title is shown at once. A host that cannot keep it upserts the old title.

archive.summary: Archive {ids, id} (vocabulary archive; id stays for 1.0 listeners).

restore.summary: Restore {ids, id} (vocabulary restore). The 1.0 name sf-thread-list-unarchive follows until 2026-12-01.

apply.summary: One of the host's row actions: {action, scope: entry, ids, id} (vocabulary apply). The 1.0 name sf-thread-list-action follows until 2026-12-01.

load-more.summary: The end came into view while has-more: {direction: after}.

toggle.summary: The archive, or the way back. The 1.0 name sf-thread-list-view follows until 2026-12-01.

updated_at.description: ISO 8601; orders the list and groups it by day.

pinned.description: Pinned (Mirai24 API v1.1): leads the list under its own heading with a quiet line saying so; pinning is the host's row action.

caption.description: A quiet second line: who it is with, the last message.

set-threads.x-summary: the whole list and whether more follows, together (§7.2 values that go together); ends a page request
set-threads.summary: Replace the list; only the conversations of the shown view (archived or not) are kept.

append-threads.x-summary: the next page; ids already shown are kept where they are
append-threads.summary: The next page, after the ones shown; a conversation already listed is not repeated.

pinned.description: Pinned (Mirai24 API v1.1): leads the list under its own heading with a quiet line saying so; pinning is the host's row action.

caption.description: A quiet second line: who it is with, the last message.

upsert.x-summary: a new or changed conversation moves where its date puts it
upsert.summary: A new or changed conversation, placed where its date puts it.

remove-thread.summary: Take one conversation off the list.

more-failed.x-summary: the next page could not be loaded: reaching the end asks again
more-failed.summary: The next page could not be loaded: reaching the end asks again.

rename.x-summary: opens the rename field in place (F2)
rename.summary: Start renaming a conversation in place, as F2 does.

open-menu.x-summary: opens the row's actions (Shift+F10, the menu key, the «⋯» button)
open-menu.summary: Open a conversation's actions, as the row's «⋯» and Shift+F10 do.

default.$comment: The Lit template in JavaScript, the migration form of §5.2 (§16).

skeleton.$comment: The threads arrive after the first paint when the host loads them: the derived skeleton (static/default/<example>.skeleton.html) holds their box until they do (standard 1.3.8 §5.4).

accessibility.x-keys: Enter and Space open the row (a native button); F2 opens the rename field, where Enter commits and Escape reverts; Shift+F10 and the menu key open the row's actions; one Tab stop for the list

aliases.$comment: Dated aliases of sf-thread-list for the shim (core/js/aliases.js, standard §16 item 20). create, rename, archive and load-more keep their DOM names (archive and load-more gain the vocabulary's ids and direction beside the old fields). setLoading and setStatus became the settings loading and status: the component reads them and notes each call (no shim row can map a method to a setting).

rows.note: {id, action} becomes {action, scope: entry, ids, id}
the setting loading; the method stays until the date and notes each call
the setting status; the method stays until the date and notes each call

x-summary: A person's conversations, newest first: grouped by day, the open one marked, renamed in place, archived or acted on through the Framework's menu, with one Tab stop and the next page asked for at the end.
x-renamed: events.sf-thread-list-select → open {id} (vocabulary §5 open); the old name a dated same-detail alias
events.sf-thread-list-unarchive → restore {ids, id} (vocabulary §5 restore); the old name a dated detail-adds alias
events.sf-thread-list-action → apply {action, scope: entry, ids, id} (vocabulary §5 apply, standard §18.3: one row's own action); the old name a dated detail-adds alias
events.sf-thread-list-view → toggle {archived}; the old name a dated same-detail alias
events archive and load-more keep their DOM names; their details gain the vocabulary's ids and direction (the old fields stay)
settings: loading and status replace setLoading() and setStatus(), which are read until 2026-12-01 and noted
entry fields: updated_at → updated-at, avatar.image_url → avatar.image-url (§18.1 kebab-case); the old spellings are read until 2026-12-01 and noted
x-decisions: version: 1.0.0 → 1.1.0, a minor while the old names hold dated aliases (§4.10).

shape (§7): a leaf. The report counts sf-avatar and sf-context-menu as placed parts; both are its own drawing -- the avatar shows a row's picture, the one context menu is the rows' shared surface, filled and opened by the list itself. No rule runs between them and no key would be bound by two writers, so keys, roles and rules would restate what the template already does (the smaller mechanism).

events (vocabulary 1.1.5 §5): create, open {id}, rename {id, title}, archive {ids}, restore {ids}, apply {action, scope: entry, ids} (§18.3: a row's own action), load-more {direction: after}, toggle {archived}. Each detail keeps the 1.0 field id beside ids, so the renamed names follow in detail-adds mode and the kept names lose nothing.
own-verb-words: none left -- action became the vocabulary's apply.

setter (§4.4): setLoading and setStatus become the settings loading and status; the methods stay until 2026-12-01 and note each call. set-threads stays an action: the list and has-more change together and a page request ends with them (§7.2 values that go together); the setting threads is the same list for a binding.
threads (§18.4): a list setting with entries {key: id, changes: content}; the rows are keyed by id, so a changed conversation redraws its own row in place and keeps the focus.
selected is a controlled value (§4.3): a press asks open {id}; the host writes selected back.

key-effects: arrows, Home and End move between rows (focus:*), Enter and Space open (select, a native button), F2 opens the rename field and Shift+F10 / the menu key the row's actions (open), as the keyboard map (row) names the actions rename and open-menu.
a11y-name: label, else the runtime word label («Разговоры»), or archive-view while the archive is shown.
item-shape: threads and actions name their fields with `of`; entry fields are kebab-case (§18.1), the 1.0 snake spellings read until the aliases' day.
template: templates.default names the Lit template js/templates/default.js, the migration form §5.2 allows.
skeleton (§5.4): the loading shape is the template's own, drawn while `loading`; its first paint is the static snapshot, and the skeleton is derived from it (presentation.skeleton.late threads).

examples: examples.json from the conversations a host shows (grouped, ungrouped, the archive, loading, empty); probe.json drives the arrows, Enter, F2, Escape and Shift+F10 and the old names (gate 16, gate 20).

css-variables: the five hooks the sheet already had, as public variables in the Framework's form, the hover and current rows each with its own (§6 a variable per state); the 1.0 --sf-thread-list--* hooks stay the internal layer.
side-effects: none. The context menu draws as sf-context-menu does (its own layer).

version 1.2.1: the first paint is retaken on ui-source c020caa: no held copy of the JSON island, no icon-font state, closed surfaces printed closed, no size the code measured; an example may declare a fake host port for gate 24's phase 3.

$comment: The list draws its glyphs as sf-icon, an unread count as sf-badge and a
conversation's picture as sf-avatar; a tag it renders is a tag it fetches. A
row's actions open in sf-context-menu on a press, so the menu is fetched after
the page is ready, and the list waits for the element before opening it. The
loading sentence is visually hidden with the sr-only utility, which a class
scan can miss on a node drawn later, so it comes with the component.

updated_at.description: ISO 8601; orders the list and groups it by day.

pinned.description: Pinned (Mirai24 API v1.1): leads the list under its own heading with a quiet line saying so; pinning is the host's row action.

caption.description: A quiet second line: who it is with, the last message.

footer.description: Under the list, after the way to the archive (a usage meter, a settings link).

threads.description: Read-only: the conversations shown, newest first.

actions.description: Row actions of the host's own, after Rename and Archive.

ai_guidance.use_when: Use sf-thread-list for a list of conversations -- an assistant's or people's chats -- the host feeds through setThreads and upsert. Promoted from simai/ui-chat sf-chat-thread-list (owner decision 2026-10-25).
do_not: Do not fetch from the element; the host answers sf-thread-list-load-more
Do not expect the list to move selected on a click; set it when the conversation is open
Do not put markup in titles or captions; they are text

accessibility.focus: One Tab stop for the list (roving tabindex: the row last moved to, else the open one, else the first). The open row carries aria-current=page and medium weight, and the system highlight in forced colours. F2 renames in place (Enter keeps, Escape gives up and does not reach a surrounding panel, leaving keeps); focus returns to the row. Shift+F10 or the menu key opens the row's actions; the «⋯» is not a Tab stop.

changes: standard simai.smart-component 1.3.8: the element is made from component.json; dated aliases in aliases.json
The first-paint snapshot's sheets.json lists the utility sheets its markup uses (retaken on ui-source 5ba9399); no behaviour changed. Nothing to change for a host.

setLoading.summary: While the first page loads: the shape of the list, and the list busy. Deprecated: the setting loading (until 2026-12-01).

setStatus.summary: A sentence in place of the list (an error); empty clears it. Deprecated: the setting status (until 2026-12-01).
